messages.text: Create projects/earth.md — the master plan for projects/earth.html — following the house planning-doc standard. Requisite sections, in order: (0) TURN/STAGE LEDGER: a table of turns/stages with status, where every future build session appends a row before touching code; (1) RELEASES: numbered release list with one-line goals; (2) per-release sections: scope (in/out), build gates (how we verify, on real devices), and backlog of deferred items; (3) FUTURE IDEAS: unscheduled parking lot; (4) IMMUTABLE WORKING RULES: mobile-first, all diagnostics in-app (never DevTools), update-plan-before-code, read-back verification after every push, no stubs or fake data; (5) DECISION LOG: dated owner decisions; (6) APPENDIX: authority order (this plan is the sole authority; chat history loses to the plan). Seed it with what is known so far about projects/earth.html and mark everything else TBD. Keep it tight and scannable on a phone.

I've set up the project's master plan with all required sections, a starter ledger entry, and the working rules locked in. Everything we don't know yet about the app is marked TBD so we can fill it in together as we decide what this app will do.

messages.text: there is a repo called Earth for the user acmeproducts. I wish to create a html5 version that has no build step no react no typescript so all assets must be acquired up front and stored in GitHub. alternatively they could be stored in the WSL instance however I don't want to have to worry about consuming too much disc space if the asset requirement is large. before we jump into it I want to consider what the different options are and what the implications are for both storage requirements and performance

Good instinct to pause before building — I've captured the four realistic asset-storage options in the plan as pending decision D1, with the storage and phone-performance tradeoffs of each. Short version: plain GitHub storage (served via GitHub Pages or jsDelivr) is free, versioned, and trivially testable on a real phone, and a typical globe-texture set is only ~5–30MB, so it wins unless a single file tops ~25–50MB; WSL has unlimited local room but your phone can't easily reach it, which clashes with our mobile-first rule.
